problem:
If $h(x)$ is left-continuous at $x=10$ and $h(10)=15,$ then

${lim}_{x\to {10}^{-}}(xh(x)-5h(10))=$
 {{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
Since $h(x)$ is left-continuous at $x=10,$ we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to {10}^{-}}h(x)=h(10)=15.
$$

Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {10}^{-}}(xh(x)-5h(10)) & ={lim}_{x\to {10}^{-}}x\cdot {lim}_{x\to {10}^{-}}h(x)-5\cdot {lim}_{x\to {10}^{-}}h(10) \\  & =10\cdot 15-5\cdot 15 \\  & =150-75 \\  & =75.\end{aligned}
$$
